audience: Practitioners who must design, operate, evaluate, and recover bounded agent systems without treating model output as authority.
outcome: The learner can deliver a provider-neutral bounded agent with typed tools, least-privilege identity, durable state, measured evaluation, privacy-conscious observability, explicit terminal outcomes, and a tested recovery runbook.

competencies: Distinguish a deterministic workflow from a model-directed loop.
Define a bounded work order, success contract, budgets, and terminal outcomes.
requiredEvidence: A work order with scope, constraints, non-goals, stop conditions, and independently testable completion evidence.

competencies: Define typed tool inputs, results, errors, side effects, approvals, and postconditions.
Keep identity, authorization, and policy enforcement outside the model.
requiredEvidence: A consequential tool contract and adversarial result table covering unauthorized, duplicate, injected, timeout, and unknown-outcome cases.

competencies: Assemble task, policy, evidence, history, and tool observations with explicit trust labels.
Measure context usefulness instead of maximizing context volume.
requiredEvidence: A context manifest with source, authority, freshness, sensitivity, inclusion reason, and removal test.

competencies: Separate working state, durable task state, learner profile, retrieved knowledge, and audit evidence.
Apply consent, retention, correction, deletion, and revalidation rules to memory.
requiredEvidence: A memory classification and lifecycle table with write authority, retention, provenance, correction, deletion, and recovery behavior.

competencies: Map host, client, server, transport, capability, identity, and data boundaries.
Treat protocol compatibility as a tested subset rather than a security guarantee.
requiredEvidence: An architecture and capability-negotiation diagram with failure and ownership boundaries.

competencies: Threat-model tools, resources, prompts, sampling, roots, elicitation, and external content.
Enforce authorization on resolved resources and preserve user control over consequential actions.
requiredEvidence: A threat model and negative-test report covering confused-deputy, prompt-injection, credential, exfiltration, and cross-boundary access cases.

competencies: Choose sequential, routing, parallel, evaluator-optimizer, or agent-loop patterns from measured requirements.
Define budgets, cancellation, checkpoints, idempotency, reconciliation, and terminal states.
requiredEvidence: A pattern decision record comparing deterministic and agent-directed orchestration against representative cases.

competencies: Define role, authority, input, output, evidence, timeout, retry, and escalation contracts for handoffs.
Reject multi-agent complexity unless measured evidence justifies it.
requiredEvidence: A typed handoff contract and equivalent-case comparison of single-agent and multi-agent designs.

competencies: Evaluate final outcomes, tool trajectories, critical safety slices, recovery, latency, cost, and human review load.
Use deterministic checks, calibrated human review, and bounded model-assisted judging appropriately.
requiredEvidence: A versioned evaluation suite with holdouts, critical gates, slice results, uncertainty, and release disposition.

competencies: Correlate agent, model, tool, state, policy, and infrastructure events without recording secrets or unnecessary content.
Detect missing telemetry and distinguish attempted, accepted, completed, failed, and unknown effects.
requiredEvidence: A redacted trace model, service objectives, alerts, telemetry-loss test, and operator diagnosis.

competencies: Classify model, prompt, retrieval, data, tool, policy, orchestration, and infrastructure failures.
Contain impact, reconcile unknown outcomes, recover safely, and convert incidents into regression evidence.
requiredEvidence: An incident timeline and recovery report with containment, reconciliation, postcondition verification, and recurrence controls.

competencies: Integrate the complete bounded-agent lifecycle into one evidence-backed release decision.
Demonstrate human authority over high-impact actions and publication.
requiredEvidence: A complete capstone evidence bundle satisfying every mastery artifact and critical rubric gate.

identity.owner: The trusted application and identity provider authenticate principals and authorize resolved resources.
identity.learnerMustDemonstrate: Separate caller, operator, workload, and delegated identities with least privilege, expiry, revocation, and audit.
identity.failureEvidence: Negative tests prove that malformed, expired, cross-tenant, over-scoped, and revoked requests fail closed.

tools.owner: A trusted executor validates, authorizes, executes, verifies, and records tool effects.
tools.learnerMustDemonstrate: Typed schemas, stable results and errors, explicit side effects, exact approvals, idempotency, bounded retry, and postconditions.
tools.failureEvidence: Fixtures cover injected output, unauthorized targets, duplicates, partial results, timeouts after possible writes, and unknown outcomes.

state.owner: The application owns durable workflow state and atomic or reconciled transitions.
state.learnerMustDemonstrate: Versioned checkpoints, ownership, concurrency control, terminal outcomes, retention, and restart behavior.
state.failureEvidence: Crash, duplicate-delivery, stale-version, partial-write, and replay tests preserve a truthful state.

memory.owner: A governed memory service owns consent, provenance, minimization, correction, retention, deletion, and revalidation.
memory.learnerMustDemonstrate: Classify working context, task state, user preferences, retrieved knowledge, and audit evidence separately.
memory.failureEvidence: Tests prevent unconsented writes, stale facts, cross-user recall, prohibited data retention, and deletion failure.

orchestration.owner: A deterministic controller owns budgets, cancellation, approvals, transitions, terminal states, and escalation.
orchestration.learnerMustDemonstrate: Choose the simplest pattern that satisfies measured requirements and make every handoff explicit.
orchestration.failureEvidence: Tests cover loop exhaustion, deadlock, lost handoff, conflicting outputs, unavailable workers, and cancellation.

evaluation.owner: A versioned evaluation service and accountable reviewers own cases, rubrics, holdouts, grading, and release gates.
evaluation.learnerMustDemonstrate: Measure outcomes, critical safety, trajectory, tools, latency, cost, coordination, recovery, and human review load.
evaluation.failureEvidence: Regression, grader-disagreement, missing-slice, contaminated-holdout, and critical-gate cases block promotion.

observability.owner: The application and platform own correlated, privacy-conscious telemetry and telemetry-health monitoring.
observability.learnerMustDemonstrate: Trace decisions and effects with identifiers, versions, timing, status, policy, and postconditions while minimizing content.
observability.failureEvidence: Tests detect dropped events, broken correlation, high-cardinality growth, secret leakage, and false completion claims.

recovery.owner: Named operators own containment, reconciliation, rollback or compensation, verification, communication, and closeout.
recovery.learnerMustDemonstrate: Recover each boundary without assuming a timeout means no side effect occurred.
recovery.failureEvidence: Exercises include unknown writes, corrupted state, bad releases, revoked access, provider failure, and incomplete compensation.

humanAuthority.owner: Authorized people retain decisions about scope, consequential actions, exceptions, learner assessment, and publication.
humanAuthority.learnerMustDemonstrate: Bind approval to the exact action and evidence, preserve refusal and escalation, and never infer authority from model confidence.
humanAuthority.failureEvidence: Tests reject stale, ambiguous, mismatched, absent, and over-broad approvals.

comparison.releaseRule: Use the least complex design that passes all critical gates and meets declared outcome, latency, cost, recovery, and review-load requirements on equivalent cases.

requiredArtifacts: bounded work order and success contract
